KEY MESSAGE 1...A strong coastal storm is expected to bring 
significant impacts to the region around Thanksgiving Day.

Following a period of relatively benign weather, our attention 
turns to the coastal storm heading towards the holiday. 
Beginning on Wednesday, the storm of concern will begin to take 
shape off the Southeast coast. A strong upper-low will shift 
eastward out of the central US, with strong divergence aloft 
favoring surface cyclogenesis over either the Southeast or off 
the coast. From there, the low is expected to track northward 
towards the Mid- Atlantic through Thursday. Guidance remains 
quite consistent on the development and rapid deepening of this 
low, though some differences still remain with respect to the 
track. With that said, the latest deterministic guidance (12z 
GFS and RGEM) still favors a more western track taking the low 
inland through the Carolinas and then continuing northward 
eventually reaching western PA. Meanwhile there's still some 
spread in the GEFS ensembles with some members tracking the low 
farther east more over the heart of our County Warning Area or 
even offshore. This all said, the overall synoptic pattern of a 
deepening upper level low over the midwestern states does favor 
a more western track. 

The chance for wintry precipitation (even at onset) appears to be 
fairly small even across the Poconos and adjacent portions of far 
northern NJ. Precipitation onset now could be as late as Thursday 
afternoon for these locations, and warm air advection will have been 
underway for quite some time by that point. This appears 
increasingly likely to be an all rain event for all locations within 
our coverage area.

Specific impacts are starting to come into better focus and at 
this point our biggest concerns are high winds and coastal 
flooding (see coastal flooding key message below). There also 
may be locally heavy rainfall leading isolated fresh water 
flooding. In terms of the winds, they will begin ramping up 
Wednesday night before peaking Thursday. Gusts of 40 to 50 mph 
are likely inland with gusts of 50 to 60 mph likely along the 
coast. In fact we've issued a High wind Watch for the Coastal 
strip for the period overnight Wednesday night through Thursday 
evening. Tree damage and power outages will be possible. Given 
recent dryness and progressive nature of this system, freshwater
flooding does not appear to be as significant of a concern, but
this threat will continue to be monitored as rainfall amounts 
come into better focus. Right now a general 1-2 inches is 
forecast. At this point though the Weather Prediction Center has
the area in a MARGINAL risk for excessive rainfall. If flooding
occurs, the main threats would be urban flooding and flooding 
of low lying areas as well as some of our more sensitive streams
and creeks. 

Timing wise, the greatest storm impacts look to be Thursday 
into Thursday night, with the low pulling away from the area on 
Friday. However even Friday there will be the potential for west
winds gusting 30 to 40 mph on the backside of the system.

Details will continue to come into better focus over the coming
days. Continue to monitor the forecast for the latest updates 
given the there likely being significant impacts to the region 
from this system over the Holiday. The rest of the Holiday 
weekend looks to feature insignificant and seasonable weather.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Significant tidal flooding is expected on 
Thursday morning. Moderate to potentially major tidal flooding 
is possible.

An impactful storm will move up the eastern seaboard on 
Wednesday into Thursday. This storm will produce quite an 
impressive fetch over water, resulting in a surge of water 
piling up along the coast. Astro tides will also be elevated, 
with the Full Moon on Tuesday. This will result in moderate to 
potentially even major flooding on Thursday morning. A Coastal 
Flood Watch was issued from the Raritan Bay, all the way down 
through the New Jersey and Delaware Atlantic coastline. The 
Watch also was issued for communities along Delaware Bay.

Confidence is rather high in at least moderate tidal flooding 
occurring. Guidance though is really spread on whether tide 
levels only get to moderate, or go into major. Some models even 
have some record breaking high tides for Thanksgiving morning, 
mainly in Cape May County, and Sussex County, NJ. If things line
up correctly, it certainly is not out of the question for not 
JUST major tidal flooding, but flooding perhaps a foot or more 
over major. If you are traveling to the coast for Thanksgiving, 
be aware of the tidal flooding potential, and follow any 
directions from local officials. Things could change in the 
other direction though, and stay firmly in moderate. Regardless,
significant tidal flooding is expected. Minor to moderate tidal
flooding could continue with Thursday Night's high tide, hence 
why the Coastal Flood Watch extends through Thursday Night.
